ticket.title: miter deps resolves a module path segment as a crate edge (outfeed_orchestrator::storypole looked like a dependency on storypole)
acceptance_criteria:
DONE 2026-11-06, commit 6abe71e (miter). Two measurement defects fixed, both found by using the tool to answer a real question rather than by reading it.

GB-290, the serious one. path_roots_in_line treated every lowercase ident:: on a line as a crate root, so `outfeed_orchestrator::storypole::gather(..)` reported a dependency on a crate named storypole. That phantom edge surfaced in the layering gate and I renamed a module to make it go away. A measurement tool that invents findings is worse than one that misses them: a miss costs nothing until someone relies on it, while an invention produces work, and the work looked justified because the report was specific.

Only the first segment of a path names a crate now. The predicate distinguishes `a::b` (later segment) from `= ::b` (path root) by looking three characters back, and three regression tests hold it: a module segment is not a crate, a root-relative path still names its crate, and a single-segment call is still counted.

GB-300. `miter impact` deduplicated by file:line:symbol - a call site - so a function reached from six sites inside another function was reported six times as an entrypoint, and the same test could appear twice. This output is what decides how large a refactor is, so a sixfold overcount makes a bounded change look unbounded. Tests and entrypoints now dedupe by symbol (the row means 'a thing to run or review'); transitive callers keep per-site detail, where the site is the fact.

Live verification: `miter impact BenchworkError` lists run_in_process_synthesis once instead of six times, with 21 distinct affected tests and no repeats.

Graph unchanged at 0 lateral, 155 downward, clean - which is the correct outcome rather than a null result: the resolver was manufacturing an edge the rename had already removed, and the rule now stops it returning.

Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, 280 tests green, audit clean, docs 9 present 0 drifted.
